# Separator

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

typography and layout · tier 1 · beta · renders on the server and ships no client JavaScript.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For a hairline between two groups: sections of a form, items of a menu, two facts on one
row. It has no margin of its own, so the gap and padding of its parent space it.

```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
  <p>Personal details</p>
  <Separator />
  <div className="flex h-5 items-center gap-3">
    <span>Draft</span>
    <Separator orientation="vertical" />
    <span>Edited 2 hours ago</span>
  </div>
</div>
```

A vertical separator takes its height from a flex or grid row, so give the row a height or
let it stretch; in a block parent it is 0 px tall. It is decorative by default and is not
announced; pass `decorative={false}` when it divides content a reader should hear as
separate, and it becomes a `separator` with its orientation.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { Separator } from 'topclassui/separator'
```

## Props

Every prop below is optional and falls back to the default shown.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `decorative` | no | `boolean` | `true` | Keeps the line out of the accessibility tree; false announces it as a separator. |
| `orientation` | no | `horizontal` \| `vertical` | `"horizontal"` | Which way the line runs: across its container, or down the height of a flex row. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
